chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Husayn ibn 'Uthman from 'Amr ibn Abi Nasr said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is it permissible for a man to speak during the Adhan?' He said, 'There is no harm.' I asked, 'And during the Iqamah?' He said, 'No.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةِ: Iqamah (the second call to prayer, immediately preceding the start of prayer)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to speak during the Adhan and Iqamah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between the Adhan and Iqamah, permitting speech during the former but prohibiting it during the latter. This ruling underscores the heightened sanctity and concentration required for the Iqamah, which immediately precedes the commencement of the prayer. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving the solemnity of the ritual calls as distinct acts of worship.
